text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.65% today as oil refining margins strengthened amid mixed signals in crude markets. Brent crude topped $106 yesterday following a Saudi airport attack, and while oil prices have since pulled back as traders weigh new Russian diesel supply against existing geopolitical tensions, U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% utilization — near full capacity — which means any stable or elevated crude prices translate directly into higher profits on the fuel they produce and sell.

The stock's 20% surge over two weeks reflects a broader tailwind: geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East (Iran fortifying nuclear sites, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure) is keeping crude prices elevated and volatile, while storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain moderate, supporting refiner margins. Even as traders debate whether new Russian diesel imports will ease global fuel costs, the current tight supply environment and high refinery utilization are working in Marathon's favor.
